summary: Model version lock cleared when response compression negotiated differently during canary window
description: Issue summary: During a staged canary rollout for redwood-v2-medium in us-east, tenants from AtlasRetail reported intermittent fallback to the legacy variant despite an explicit model version pin. Impact: customer-facing churn of generated outputs, increased token usage as requests hit fallback variant, and two 5xx errors observed in the tenant's request stream. Environment: production (us-east-1), customer uses Dedicated plan with model pin on their route. Steps to reproduce: 1) Call the customer's pinned route with Accept-Encoding: br,gzip;q=0.8 2) Send several warmup chat completions with streaming enabled 3) Observe whether the response stream continues under pinned model or switches to fallback Observed behavior: When the edge-proxy and sidecar disagreed on response compression (edge selected brotli, sidecar decompressed and recompressed as gzip), the cookie used for model-pin (route_pin_v2) was sometimes cleared on response path. This leads the orchestrator to consider the session unpinned and route to the canary fallback. Expected behavior: Pin cookie should be preserved across response compression negotiation and not be cleared by intermediate components. Logs / artifacts: - Edge logs: "WARN edge: client_accept_encoding=br negotiation=sidecar_gzip set-cookie: route_pin_v2=; Expires=Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:00 GMT" - Sidecar trace: "compression: decompress br -> recompress gzip; response-headers sanitized; set-cookie removed by header-sanitizer v2.1" - Customer repro curl: curl -i -H 'Accept-Encoding: br' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <cust-token>' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/route/atlas-chat/complete
investigation_notes: 03-10 14:05 UTC — Support triaged; impact confirmed for ~12 unique tenant sessions; spike coincided with canary weight bump to 7%.

03-10 14:22 UTC — SRE reproduced locally by sending br-encoded streaming responses through edge proxy with header-sanitizer enabled; observed set-cookie deletion when sanitizer runs after compression negotiation.

Hypothesis: header-sanitizer rule designed to drop large cookies was triggered because brotli produced compressed chunk metadata that contained the cookie name in a trailing frame; sanitizer matched pattern and cleared cookie header.

Edge difference: new edge-proxy v3.12 introduced brotli-first negotiation for lower-latency clients; sidecars on older Dedicated hosts still operate gzip-first. Mismatch increases header rewriting passes.
Relevant metrics: pin_evictions_per_min on us-east spiked from baseline 0.2 to 4.1 at 14:10 UTC; fallback_rate for atlas-chat route rose from 0.3% to 8.7%.
Attached artifacts: support bundle archive (s3://support-bundles/SUP-202840/), edge log excerpts, sidecar trace ids: trace-edge-63512, trace-sidecar-63514.
Cross-ref Slack: #support thread https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C03SUPPORT/p167847... and incident channel #inc-2026-canary-compression for live updates.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use customer route with explicit model pin (AtlasRetail route) in prod us-east
2) Send streaming completion requests with Accept-Encoding: br header
3) Monitor response headers for Set-Cookie: route_pin_v2 being present or removed
4) Toggle header-sanitizer flag on proxy to reproduce removal behavior
comments: 2026-03-10 14:12 — Aisha Patel (Support): Customer reports 'we see occasional outputs from older model and our logs show a pin cookie being unset on 200 responses'. Asked for sample request IDs.

2026-03-10 14:30 — Linh Tran (SRE): Reproduced in staging with edge-proxy v3.12 + sidecar v2.9. Header-sanitizer rule 'cookie-size-prune' removes cookies when compressed frames include 'Set-Cookie' token; creating patch to change sanitizer ordering.

2026-03-10 15:05 — Diego Morales (Eng): Deployed temporary edge-proxy config rollback (disabled brotli-first negotiation) for the atlas cluster to keep negotiation stable. Early telemetry shows pin_evictions fell back to baseline.
2026-03-10 15:45 — Customer (Jordan Kim, AtlasRetail): Confirmed that fallbacks stopped after rollback; provided 4 example request IDs where mismatch previously happened.

2026-03-11 09:20 — Diego Morales (Eng): Merged fix in edge-proxy PR to ensure header-sanitizer runs before compression rewriter and to whitelist route_pin_v2 cookie names. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/4382

2026-03-12 11:00 — Aisha Patel (Support): Verified with customer that behavior is resolved and no further regressions observed. Marking issue resolved; follow-up task created for canary gating checks.
resolution: Short-term mitigation: rolled back brotli-first negotiation in us-east routing plane for affected fleet at 2026-03-10 15:00 UTC to stabilize compression behavior.

Applied fix: edge-proxy change to sanitizer ordering + cookie whitelist merged and deployed to staging; rollout to prod scheduled after canary gating (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/4382).
Customer workaround (if seen in future): include Accept-Encoding: gzip in client calls as a temporary measure to avoid negotiation mismatch.

Post-incident follow-ups: 1) Add unit tests for header-sanitizer to preserve known pin cookie names across compression rewriters. 2) Add a canary gating check that validates Set-Cookie persistence for pinned routes during protocol/feature changes. 3) Create a small dashboard alert for pin_evictions_per_min > 1.0 for enterprise routes.
